misconceptions.description: Believing that hand-rewording AI output removes the need to disclose AI assistance
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits reworded AI text and reports that no AI was used
misconceptions.feedback: Disclosure is about where the ideas and drafting help came from, not the exact words. If AI shaped the content, the AI-use note must say so even after you reword it.

misconceptions.description: Assuming every course and assignment allows the same AI use
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites a different course's AI rule to justify use in this assignment
misconceptions.feedback: AI rules are set per assignment and per syllabus. Check this assignment's stated policy before using AI, and ask the instructor when it is unclear.

misconceptions.description: Treating grammar fixes and full-answer generation as the same level of allowed AI help
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses AI to produce the substantive answer when only proofreading was permitted
misconceptions.feedback: Separate proofreading and formatting (often allowed) from generating ideas or answers (often restricted). Match your use to what the assignment permits.
